To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the simulation of proton transport in matter in the energy range of interest, i.e., up to 65 MeV is affected by several epistemic uncertainties.
the epistemic uncertainties of the models implemented in the Geant 4 toolkit are of the order of 10% in the range of energies of interest for proton radiotherapy.
the simulation of proton transport in matter is subject to several sources of physics-related epistemic uncertainties.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the assessment and the quantification of the physics uncertainties affecting the simulation of proton depth dose distributions in matter, with a view to the application in the field of proton radiotherapy.
the assessment of the physics-related uncertainties of the models implemented in the Geant 4 toolkit, and their impact on the simulation results of the energy deposition of protons in matter.

the physics models used in Geant4 for the simulation of proton depth dose in matter, and the related epistemic uncertainties; it aims to provide a quantitative assessment of the features of such models and the impact on the simulation results of the uncertainties associated with them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the simulation of proton depth doses in the range up to approximately 65 MeV is sufficiently accurate to be used in the context of experimental studies in proton therapy, but that the simulation of dose profiles in the entrance region is not.
, for a large number of the models considered, the uncertainties are not negligible in the context of radiotherapy applications.

, in spite of the fact that the Geant4 physics list is a very powerful tool, its use should be done with great care, and the user should be aware of the uncertainties and limitations that the physics list introduces.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Geant4 is a very useful tool for proton dose calculations.
, in the energy range of interest, the simulation of energy deposition in matter by means of the models implemented in Geant4 is accurate within a few per cent.

Geant4 models are able to simulate the physics of proton energy deposition with a level of accuracy that is sufficient for the majority of applications in proton radiotherapy, provided that the uncertainties are taken into account.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in order to achieve the highest level of precision and accuracy in the simulation of proton dose distributions in the energy range under study, it is crucial to account for the epistemic uncertainties of the physics models and parameters.

, while the physics models and parameters implemented in Geant4 are in good agreement with the available experimental data and with the recommendations of the ICRU, the associated uncertainties are large enough to affect the simulation results significantly, especially in the case of radiotherapy set-up simulation.
the epistemic uncertainties of the models considered are relevant in the context of radiotherapy applications and that they should be taken into account in the interpretation of the results.
